topic: Reddi Kingdoms of Kondavidu & Rajahmundry (with the Gajapatis)

items.title: Post-Kakatiya Andhra: Musunuris, Velamas & Reddis
items.body:
## The vacuum after 1323

- The **Kakatiya empire fell in 1323** when the Delhi Sultanate captured **Prataparudra II** and renamed Warangal 'Sultanpur'. Tughluq control soon proved **tenuous**, and local Telugu chieftains seized power.
- Three warrior lineages rose out of the chaos:

| Lineage | Core region | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Musunuri Nayakas** | Coastal Andhra → Warangal | Led the anti-Sultanate revolt |
| **Recherla Velamas** | Telangana (Rachakonda, Devarakonda) | Rivals of the Reddis |
| **Reddis** | Coastal & central Andhra (Kondavidu) | Longest-lasting of the three |

## The Musunuri Nayakas

- **Prolaya Nayaka** appeared c.1330 at Rekapalle claiming Kakatiya heritage and issued the **Vilasa copper-plate grant** near Pithapuram, lamenting the devastation of the Telugu country.
- His cousin **Kapaya Nayaka (r.1333–1368)** led a wider rising and **recovered Warangal from the Tughluqs in 1336**, said to be aided by **75 Nayakas** (Prolaya Vema Reddi among them).
- Kapaya was later pressed by the Bahmanis and **overthrown by the Recherla Velamas in 1368**.
keyPoints: Kakatiya empire ended 1323 (capture of Prataparudra II); Warangal renamed Sultanpur.
Three Telugu lineages filled the vacuum: Musunuri Nayakas, Recherla Velamas, Reddis.
Prolaya Nayaka issued the Vilasa grant (c.1330) near Pithapuram.
Kapaya Nayaka recovered Warangal from the Tughluqs in 1336, aided by 75 Nayakas.
Musunuri power fell to the Recherla Velamas in 1368.

items.title: The Reddi Kingdom of Kondavidu — Foundation & Rulers
items.body:
## Origins of the Reddis

- The word **'Reddi'** (earlier Rattakudi / Rattodi, linked to **Rashtrakuta**) meant a **village headman** who organised cultivation and collected taxes. The founder's ancestors held the post of **sainya-nayaka** (military commander) under the Kakatiyas.
- **Prolaya Vema Reddi** of the **Panta Reddi clan** set up independent rule around **1325**, with his first capital at **Addanki**.

## Line of Kondavidu rulers

- **Prolaya Vema Reddi (r.c.1325–1353)** — founder; a great temple-builder, titled **Apratima-Bhudana-Parasurama**; patron of the poet **Errana**.
- **Anavota (Anapota) Reddi** — consolidated the state and shifted the capital to the strong hill-fort of **Kondavidu** (Guntur district).
- **Anavema Reddi** — extended trade; abolished customs/trade duties.
- **Kumaragiri Reddi (r.c.1386–1402)** — scholar-king; wrote the dance treatise **Vasantarajiyam**.
- **Peda Komati Vema Reddi** — patron of **Srinatha**; himself a scholar.

> Exam trap: distinguish **Prolaya Vema Reddi** (the founder, patron of Errana) from **Peda Komati Vema Reddi** (a later Kondavidu king, patron of Srinatha).
keyPoints: 'Reddi' derives from Rattakudi/Rashtrakuta — village headmen; founder's line were sainya-nayakas under the Kakatiyas.
Prolaya Vema Reddi (Panta clan) founded the kingdom c.1325 with Addanki as first capital.
Anavota Reddi shifted the capital to the Kondavidu hill-fort (Guntur district).
Kumaragiri Reddi (r.c.1386–1402) authored the dance treatise Vasantarajiyam.
Prolaya Vema Reddi patronised Errana; Peda Komati Vema Reddi patronised Srinatha.
items.mnemonic: Two 'Vema' patrons: Prolaya Vema → Errana; Peda Komati Vema → Srinatha.
items.source: Wikipedia — Reddy Kingdom; History & Culture of the Andhras (Telugu Akademi)

items.title: Rajahmundry Branch, Forts & Extent
items.body:
## The Rajahmundry Reddis

- A **subsidiary branch was established around 1395 at Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram)** and later became independent.
- Its rulers included **Kataya Vema Reddi, Allada Reddi** (a powerful regent) and **Virabhadra Reddi**, the last of whom patronised **Srinatha** in his later years.

## Forts and extent

- The Reddis were famed **fort-builders**. The two great surviving hill-forts are **Kondavidu** (about 30 km west of Guntur) and **Kondapalli** (about 20 km north-west of Vijayawada).
- The **Palnadu** forts of **Bellamkonda, Vinukonda and Nagarjunakonda** also formed part of the kingdom.
- At its height the kingdom stretched from **Cuttack (Odisha) in the north to Kanchi in the south, with Srisailam to the west**, its core lying between the **Krishna and Godavari** rivers.
keyPoints: A Reddi branch was set up at Rajahmundry c.1395 and later became independent.
Rajahmundry rulers: Kataya Vema, Allada Reddi and Virabhadra Reddi (patron of Srinatha).
Chief Reddi forts: Kondavidu (west of Guntur) and Kondapalli (near Vijayawada).
Palnadu forts Bellamkonda, Vinukonda and Nagarjunakonda were also Reddi.
Maximum extent: Cuttack (N) to Kanchi (S), Srisailam (W); core between Krishna and Godavari.

items.title: Reddi Administration, Trade & Religion
items.body:
## Administration & economy

- Government was conducted according to the **Dharmasutras**. The state took **one-sixth of the agricultural surplus** as land tax.
- Under **Anavota / Anavema Reddi, customs and trade duties were lifted**, so commerce flourished; **sea trade passed through the port of Motupalli**, which drew a large merchant settlement.

## Religion

- The Reddis were **staunch patrons of Hinduism** — restoring Brahmin **agraharas**, encouraging Vedic studies, and endowing the temples of **Srisailam, Tirumala, Ahobilam and Vontimitta**.
- **Prolaya Vema Reddi** built a **flight of steps** from the Krishna River to the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** temple, repaired that shrine, built the **Ahobilam Narasimha** temple and is credited with **108 Siva temples**.
- The dynasty's **kula-devi (tutelary goddess) was Mullamguramma**, a village goddess later identified with **Uma (Parvati)**.
keyPoints: Administration followed the Dharmasutras; land tax was one-sixth of the surplus.
Anavota/Anavema Reddi abolished customs/trade duties, boosting commerce.
Sea trade flowed through the port of Motupalli.
Reddis endowed Srisailam, Tirumala, Ahobilam and Vontimitta temples and Brahmin agraharas.
Kula-devi of the Reddis was Mullamguramma, later identified with Uma/Parvati.

items.title: Telugu Literature under the Reddis — Errana & Srinatha
items.body:
## A golden age of Telugu letters

Telugu (and Sanskrit) literature blossomed under Reddi patronage; several kings were themselves authors.

### Errana (Errapragada)

- **Court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddi** and the **third member of the Kavitraya** (Nannaya–Tikkana–Errana).
- **Completed the Aranya Parva** of the Telugu Mahabharata left unfinished by Nannaya; bridged Nannaya's and Tikkana's styles.
- Also wrote **Nrisimha Puranamu** and **Harivamsamu**; titles **'Prabandha Parameswara'** and **'Sambhudasa'**.

### Srinatha — the colossus

- Served as **Vidyadhikari (education officer) at Kondavidu under Peda Komati Vema Reddi**.
- Won the title **'Kavi Sarvabhauma'** (Emperor of Poets) and a **Kanakabhishekam** (shower of gold) at the **Vijayanagara court of Praudha Devaraya**, after defeating the scholar **Dindima Bhattu**.
- Works: **Sringara Naishadhamu** (from Sri Harsha's Naishadhiya Charitam), **Bhimakhandamu, Kasikhandamu, Haravilasamu** and the dwipada **Palnati Vira Charitra**. He later served the Rajahmundry Reddi **Virabhadra**.
- **Bammera Potana**, author of the Telugu **Bhagavatamu**, also belonged to this age.
keyPoints: Errana, court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddi, completed the Aranya Parva and is the third of the Kavitraya.
Errana's titles: Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa; works Nrisimha Puranamu and Harivamsamu.
Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at Kondavidu under Peda Komati Vema Reddi.
Srinatha won 'Kavi Sarvabhauma' and Kanakabhishekam at Praudha Devaraya's Vijayanagara court.
Srinatha's works: Sringara Naishadhamu, Bhimakhandamu, Kasikhandamu, Palnati Vira Charitra.
items.source: History & Culture of the Andhras (Telugu Akademi / APPSC reference), Literature

items.title: Decline of the Reddis & the Gajapatis of Kalinga
items.body:
## End of the Reddi kingdoms

- Squeezed between **Vijayanagara**, the **Recherla Velamas–Bahmani** combine and the **Gajapatis**, the Reddis declined in the 15th century.
- **Kondavidu was annexed by the Vijayanagara Empire in 1424**; the **Rajahmundry branch was conquered by the Gajapatis of Odisha around 1448**, closing the c.1325–1448 span.

## The Gajapatis of Odisha (Kalinga)

- Founded by **Kapilendra Deva in 1434** (Suryavamsa line) after the end of the **Eastern Gangas**; capital at **Kataka (Cuttack)**.
- **'Gajapati' (lord of elephants)** was one of the **four royal titles** of medieval India — the others being **Narapati** (Vijayanagara), **Aswapati** (Bahmani sultans) and **Chhatrapati**.
- Ardent **Vaishnavas**, they expanded the **Jagannath cult** of Puri; **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu** influenced Emperor **Prataparudra Deva**.
- The Gajapatis briefly held **coastal Andhra** (including former Reddi Rajahmundry) but lost it when **Prataparudra Deva was defeated by Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara**.
keyPoints: Kondavidu annexed by Vijayanagara in 1424; Rajahmundry taken by the Gajapatis c.1448.
Reddi kingdom's overall span was c.1325–1448.
Gajapati kingdom founded by Kapilendra Deva (1434), capital Kataka (Cuttack).
'Gajapati' was one of four royal titles: Gajapati, Narapati, Aswapati, Chhatrapati.
Gajapatis expanded the Jagannath cult; Prataparudra Deva was defeated by Krishnadevaraya.
